cands.name: Rudolph Valentino Drake

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.

cands.bio: Democratic candidate for Alabama State Senate District 2. Born in Huntsville and raised in Harvest. Served in the U.S. Navy in aviation quality assurance, then worked as a Department of Defense Police Officer and in aviation leadership supporting aircraft operations. No prior elected office found.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists him as recommended in three Sway voter guides: How Clay Votes, Tabitha's List: Candidates You Can Trust, and Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy. These are voter-guide recommendations, not organizational endorsements.

cands.gaps: We found no record of any prior elected office or legislative work. His campaign site lists priorities (affordable healthcare, lower cost of living, and improving education) but gives no specific positions on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, guns, abortion, policing or school choice. We found no documented actions on those topics. He did not complete Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey. We could not find his birth year, the dates of his Navy service, or the names of his employers. We found no documented controversies and no foreign ties.

cands.name: John Roberts

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Republican from Huntsville, Alabama, running for State Senate District 2. Former Director of Government Affairs at the Huntsville Madison County Builders Association and Business Retention & Expansion Director at the Huntsville/Madison County Chamber. Now Real Estate & Development Manager at Freedom Real Estate & Capital. Co-founded the North Alabama Homebuilding Academy.
cands.gaps: We found no record of Roberts holding elected office, so there are no legislative actions to report. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, and no endorsements were listed for this race. We found no documented stance from him on data centers or on specific development projects. His site mentions attracting investment in artificial intelligence but says nothing about data centers. We found nothing specific from him on homestead property taxes beyond a general promise of lower taxes and less wasteful spending. We also found nothing from him on immigration or H-1B, police, guns, abortion, or teacher pay raises. We found no news coverage of controversies, and no foreign ties.
